title: HTTP media response
responsibility: Serves media bytes as a full response or a single validated byte range.

inputs.name: mediaResponse.bytes
inputs.description: The Node.js Buffer containing the complete media body; its length sets the full-response length and range bounds. Valid ranges are sliced from this buffer.

inputs.name: mediaResponse.mime
inputs.description: The string used for the response's Content-Type header, which identifies the media to clients. It is passed directly to Headers, so invalid HTTP header values can throw TypeError.

inputs.name: mediaResponse.range
inputs.description: When omitted (default undefined), null, or empty, the helper returns the full buffer; otherwise this is one bytes=...-... range. It accepts closed, open-ended, or positive suffix ranges and returns 416 for malformed, unsafe-integer, or unsatisfiable ranges; multiple ranges are unsupported.

inputs.name: mediaResponse.disposition
inputs.description: The string used as the response's Content-Disposition header to set client presentation behavior. It defaults to inline and is passed directly to Headers, so invalid HTTP header values can throw TypeError.

outputs.name: mediaResponse
outputs.description: Returns a Fetch Response with Content-Type, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Cache-Control: no-store, Content-Disposition, and Accept-Ranges: bytes headers. A falsy range yields status 200 with all bytes and Content-Length; a valid single range yields status 206 with the selected bytes, Content-Range, and selected-byte Content-Length, while a malformed or unsatisfiable nonempty range yields status 416, a null body, and Content-Range: bytes */<total-size>.

errors.name: TypeError
errors.description: Constructing Headers throws TypeError if the supplied mime or disposition is not a valid HTTP header value. This exception is not caught, so the function returns no Response.
